This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **18** documentable anchor(s).

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **213** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **153** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **153**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **98** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **42** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c658320792a49b2741335667f7163f5460b2fddd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `14d0df6538380c7713e639f981caf04e4dddbf16` — the merge of head `b8f5998e74eb18300aaa679a643bdd9fb066162c` into base `c658320792a49b2741335667f7163f5460b2fddd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 14d0df6538380c7713e639f981caf04e4dddbf16 && git checkout 14d0df6538380c7713e639f981caf04e4dddbf16
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c658320792a49b2741335667f7163f5460b2fddd b8f5998e74eb18300aaa679a643bdd9fb066162c && git checkout -B drift-repro c658320792a49b2741335667f7163f5460b2fddd && git merge --no-ff b8f5998e74eb18300aaa679a643bdd9fb066162c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c658320792a49b2741335667f7163f5460b2fddd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c658320792a49b2741335667f7163f5460b2fddd` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b8f5998e74eb18300aaa679a643bdd9fb066162c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.packageless-layered-read-refusal.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.read-verb-canonical-fold.test.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts, packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-layers-ambiguous-package.test.ts, packages/rest/src/execctx-consumer-census.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-layers-ambiguous-package.test.ts, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-environment-rows.ts (`packagelessAddress`, `packagelessContentPackage`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-lock-version-gates.ts (`packagelessReadAddress`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts at `servedOverlayRowCandidates` and `getMetaItemLayered` on `main`, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts (`GetMetaItemLayeredRequestSchema`), packages/spec/src/api/plugin-rest-api.zod.ts (the `/:type/:name/layers` row), docs/adr/0146 D2/D8/D11, packages/objectql/src/protocol-custom-override-effective-read.test.ts (the #28507 pin), ui/packages/data-objectstack/src/metadata-client.ts (`layered`), ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/ResourceEditPage.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/ObjectListViewInspector.tsx, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/check-engine-double-contract.mjs

Face: `record-recognisers --paths` over the twelve committed paths decides no face on its own (no published-schema path, no governed register row; `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` is a gate ledger, not a governed surface) and defers to the changeset's `Clause-②:` line, which carries the `(narrowing)` arm, so the narrowing face at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` is the one owed, and this record is the complete ①–④ for it. The PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no author note is owed under ③.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Which reads move from 200 to 409, exactly.** The new judge `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.packagelessLayeredReadRefusal` calls `packagelessAddress(type, name, member)` at `state: 'active'` and refuses only when `address.candidates` holds two or more ids. Read against `packagelessAddress` in `protocol-environment-rows.ts`: `candidates` is the set of distinct non-empty `package_id` values among the item's ACTIVE rows at the addressed member; a row with no package sets `unbound` and is never a candidate; draft rows are at another `state` and never read. So the set of newly refused requests is precisely: a layered read naming no package (`?package=` absent, empty, or `all`, which `metaItemPackageBinding` folds to no package on both transports, exactly as the writes fold it) of a name whose active rows two or more packages hold. Correct against the ruling. Not refused, and pinned by `protocol.packageless-layered-read-refusal.test.ts` (second case): one package's row alone; one package's row with the package-unbound row beside it; the package-unbound row alone; no row. Correct.
- **The `.custom` pair is not caught, and the #28507 design is not regressed.** Under ADR-0146 D8 the base is a CODE artifact the loader registered (`installPackage`, as the #28507 pin `protocol-custom-override-effective-read.test.ts` builds it), and the declared override is a stored row of the base's `.custom` pair. `packagelessAddress` reads stored rows only, so for that shape `candidates` is the one pair id, the judge answers `undefined`, and the layered read proceeds to `packagelessReadAddress`, where `packagelessContentPackage` sees one shipper (the base) and addresses the read to the base, under which `servedOverlayRowCandidates` serves the pair's declared override first: the #28507 answer, untouched. The pin's own "beside a package-unbound row, the declared override is served, where a save naming no package now writes" case is likewise one candidate. The only `.custom` shape that is refused is a base's own STORED row beside its pair's row, which is two bindings for the package-less save already (the #28507 docblock on `servedOverlayRowCandidates` states the pair-row rule only "whenever it is the item's only binding"), so the read now answers exactly what that save answers. That shape has no designed producer (the ensure door of #28512 opens a pair for a read-only base, whose items the write door seals; a writable Studio package is edited in place and gets no pair), and ADR-0146 D11 closes the package-less write on packaged names anyway. Judged correct, not a regression.
- **Same judge, same code, status, holders field and message family as the writes.** `packagelessAddressAmbiguityRefusal` is the one constructor the direct save (`protocol.ts` at the publish-mode address check and the authoring draft path), the per-item publish and the delete already throw; the PR widens its `verb` union by `'layered read'` and adds the matching "Nothing was served." / "no single row to show" pair, leaving every other field (the `409`, `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, the sorted holder list, the `?package=` prescription first) to the shared body. No exhaustive switch elsewhere reads the verb (the only callers are the five throw sites and this one). The protocol test pins `code` and `status` equal to the thrown save refusal's and the full sentence. Correct: called, not restated.
- **`/layers` and `?layers=true` agree, on both doors.** On `RestServer` the deprecated flag folds into the same `/layers` handler, which calls `createMetaLayeredAnswer` once (the only other caller of the chain is the runtime dispatcher's `answerMetaLayered`); `/published` does not go through this chain (it calls `getMetaItemLayered` directly), so its "keeps serving" claim holds. The REST test exercises both spellings against the same `PUT` and `DELETE` and compares status, code and envelope keys; the runtime test does the same through the real `HttpDispatcher.dispatch()` with both spellings, each door compared with its own `PUT`. Correct.
- **`?package=` path unchanged.** Step 1c is guarded by `if (!packageId)`, and `getMetaItemLayered` naming a package is untouched; pinned on both spellings and both doors. Correct.
- **`sys-metadata-repository.ts`**: the verb union and the two wording strings only; the docblock gains the layered read as a fourth reader of the one refusal. The repository's own `put` address refusal (its `'save'` throw) is untouched. Correct.
- **`engine-double-contract.pinned.json`**: the two new tests build an in-memory engine double that reaches `assertEngineDeleteDispatch`, `assertEngineUpdateDispatch` and `assertEngineFindOnePredicate` (the declared-contract admission route of `check-engine-double-contract.mjs`), so the ledger gains exactly three rows per file, `pinned: 1`; the runtime test uses real better-sqlite3 and is correctly absent. A `--write` regeneration whose diff is exactly the doubles the PR adds is the legitimate shape; no existing row moves. Correct.
- **Both doors wired the same way.** `RestServer.metaItemReadGateSources` and the dispatcher's `metaItemReadGateSources` hand the protocol's judge through only when it is a function (`RestProtocol` and `MetaDomainProtocol` gain it as an optional member), so a protocol without the judge answers as before; both transports now pass `member` (`metaMemberSelector(req.query)` / the dispatcher's `memberSelector`) into `MetaLayeredRequest`, and the judge resolves it through `resolveBundleMemberSelector` before `packagelessAddress`, the same resolution the save's `itemDiscriminator` feeds. Correct.
- **Scope of types**: the save's address check is type-agnostic (`mode === 'publish'`, no package, no `source`, not `package-duplicate`), as is the delete's; the judge is asked on every type the layered door serves, including `object` (step 1b's `object` exemption is 1b's, not 1c's). The read refuses exactly where the writes refuse. Correct.
- **Census pins**: `protocol.read-verb-canonical-fold.test.ts` derives the fold population and the judge calls `canonicalizeMetaRequestType` first, so it joins ("nineteen"); `execctx-consumer-census.test.ts`'s Proxy fake answers the judge `undefined` so the `/layers` row still measures what it measured. Correct, and the dev's account of the first red run matches the diff.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` with `Metadata-protocol: none` and three `patch` entries (`@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`), on the PR body and the changeset alike. Under ruling A as `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` mechanizes it, the level follows the `Metadata-protocol:` kind alone: `none` must grade every introduced entry `patch`, which it does, and a non-protocol narrowing "ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and its ADR-0087 disposition" — the `!` in the title and the `**BREAKING**` banner are those carriers, not a level claim. `none` is right: no key of a schema moves, no `authorable-surface/` or `authorable-defaults/` baseline moves; what moves is a REST door's answer. The `(narrowing)` arm is the ADR-0087 breaking signal, so `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` owes exactly one disposition marker, which the changeset carries: `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with its reason; the body carries no `FROM`/`TO` placeholder, no arrow rewrite and no migration-framed heading, so the detector's one mechanical check holds, and the argument (the remedy is the request's `?package=`, nothing stored changes) is the category's. The new public members (`packagelessLayeredReadRefusal` on the class, optional on `RestProtocol`, `MetaItemReadGateSources` and `MetaDomainProtocol`, `member` on `MetaLayeredRequest`, `'layered read'` in the verb union) are additive. Consistent.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Studio seam (the dev's flag): judged, and it is a ui follow-up card, not an in-PR fix.** Read in `ui/`: `MetadataClient.layered(type, name, { packageId?, member? })` already takes the package. `ResourceEditPage.tsx` passes `ownerPackageId` whenever it knows the owner (its load, refresh and after-save reads), so the main item editor is scoped and sees no change. The package-less callers are `PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx` (`client.layered(type, name)` with a swallowing `catch`, and two sibling reads; permission sets hold one name per deployment under ADR-0146, so two package holders is the ambiguity publish already refuses) and `ObjectListViewInspector.tsx` (`client.layered('view', viewId)`, object-qualified view ids, inside the panel's own `try`). In a single-install flow nothing changes; where two installed packages hold one name, the save those surfaces would send next was already refused with this code. Nothing here is a shipped flow this PR breaks that the server PR could repair: the order forbids `ui/**` edits, the fix is to pass the owning package (or surface the prescription) at those call sites, and the dev's `Seam:` line names them. The seat should file the ui card citing this record with the three call sites above; not a must-fix.
- **Step order 1b before 1c, with a disabled holder.** Step 1b (`isItemOfDisabledPackage`) asks the package-less `getMetaItem`, whose row for a two-holder name is still the silent pick; when one holder is disabled and the pick meets it, 1b answers the absence (404) before 1c's 409, so for that one corner the read's refusal reason can depend on the pick, while the package-less write answers 409 (`packagelessAddress` counts a disabled package's row). Both are refusals, the card's measured scenario (two enabled holders) is deterministic and pinned, and 1b's pick-dependence predates this PR, so this is a boundary, not a must-fix: a follow-up may move 1c ahead of 1b, or ask 1b at the resolved address. Noted, no card owed by this record.
- **The plain item read and `/published` keep the best-effort first match** for a two-holder name, by design and by the ruling's scope (`/layers` only); ADR-0146 D8 already states that "first match is no longer an answer" and routes the rest through N-03/N-09/N-16. Not this PR's to widen.
- **Check-runs on this head were in progress at the time of this read** (Build Core, the eight Test Core shards, the lint and type-check lanes, Live E2E UI; 14 successes, none failed). The all-green leg is the seat's before enqueue, not this record's.
- **Overlap.** `git merge-tree` of this head against `origin/main` (which now carries #28512) is clean. Against open #28554's head: `protocol.ts` auto-merges (that PR adds the override write gate; it does not touch `packagelessAddress` or the layered read) and the only conflict is `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`, both sides appending ledger rows; whichever lands second regenerates the ledger with `--write` and reconciles. Textual only.
- The dev's `open_questions` is empty; its `out_of_scope_findings` are the two items above, answered here.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published spec on `main`: `GetMetaItemLayeredRequestSchema` declares `packageId` optional, "scopes the `code` layer so a same-name collision resolves to the requested package's artifact (ADR-0048)", and the route row declares a diagnostic projection with its own response schema; neither promises an answer for a name the request cannot address, and ADR-0048 §3.3's "best-effort first match" sentence for a context-free read is the one ADR-0146 D8 supersedes ("first match is no longer an answer for a read carrying a type and a name"). The refusal takes no declared capability away at the consumer: the capability the spec declares — read one package's stack by naming it — is untouched, and what is removed is an undeclared coin toss that misled the editor into a save the writes then refused. It makes the writes' own refusal real at the read, with one judge over one resolution, which is the contract-first shape AGENTS.md asks for (reject loudly at the door rather than tolerate at the consumer). The placement is right: at the door (`createMetaLayeredAnswer`), with the thrown refusal reaching each transport's existing catch so the envelope is the save door's, and not inside `getMetaItemLayered`, whose in-process readers (the security catalog echo, the packaged-permission-set lock gate, `/published`) the ruling does not name; the protocol test pins that in-process reader explicitly. The `.custom` pair of ADR-0146 is served through a code base plus one stored pair row, which is one binding, so the narrowing does not reach the override design; where it reaches a base's own stored row beside its pair, it refuses where the save already refuses, which D11 closes anyway. The pin regeneration is the ledger's documented route for a declared-contract double. The change holds against the code it cites and the scenario it is accepted against.
